profile.reading: QTS Richmond 2 (RIC2) is a data center campus in Sandston, Virginia, just east of Richmond and immediately adjacent to Richmond International Airport, developed by QTS Realty Trust (formerly Quality Technology Services, renamed following the company's 2013 IPO; this registry tracks both names as the same operator). Per QTS's own site, the campus spans approximately 85 acres and is planned to include five buildings once fully built out, with a total planned capacity of 180 megawatts of IT power upon completion; that figure describes the campus as a whole rather than any single building, and much of it was not yet in operation as of the source page, so it is not applied here as this building's own confirmed capacity. This building, DC6, sits at 6070 Technology Boulevard, one of five addressed buildings running along Technology Boulevard: 6030 (DC1), 6040 (DC2), 6050 (DC3), 6060 (DC5), and 6070 (DC6); the campus's own numbering skips DC4 entirely, a naming gap this registry notes rather than attempts to explain. RIC2 is QTS's second Richmond-area campus, distinct from the company's original Richmond 1 (RIC1) campus elsewhere in the metro, which this registry documents as a separate set of facilities. Henrico County, where Sandston sits, has become one of the mid-Atlantic's fastest-growing data center corridors in recent years, drawing hyperscale and colocation development on the strength of available land, Dominion Energy transmission capacity, and dense regional fiber routes running through the Richmond area. QTS's own campus page does not state which, if any, of the five RIC2 buildings are currently operating versus still under construction, and does not publish individual square footage, IT capacity, or year-opened figures for any single building on the campus; none of those figures is asserted here for DC6 specifically, consistent with this registry's practice of reporting only what the operator has actually confirmed at the building level.

reading.body:
QTS Richmond 2 is a planned data center campus on approximately 85 acres in Sandston, Virginia, immediately adjacent to Richmond International Airport and east of Richmond. The operator has published that the campus will eventually comprise five buildings with a total planned capacity of 180 megawatts of IT power upon full completion. DC6, located at 6070 Technology Boulevard, is one of five addressed buildings on the campus; the operator's public specification page does not state which buildings are currently operating versus under construction, nor does it publish individual capacity figures for any single building.

The campus sits in Henrico County, a mid-Atlantic corridor that has drawn hyperscale and colocation development. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities statewide, of which 23 have published megawatt figures totaling 1,375 megawatts; this campus's planned 180-megawatt figure, if fully realized and recognized as a single campus total, would rank it 24th among all published capacity in the state, though that figure describes eventual full completion rather than current operating load.

The operator has not published which certifications or compliance standards apply to individual RIC2 buildings. Because the operator has not disclosed how the planned 180 megawatts of IT load is distributed across the five buildings, or which buildings are now operating, DC6's present relevance to AI infrastructure scaling cannot be determined from the published record.
